programmes.description: Nemausus 1, designed by Jean Nouvel in Nîmes during the 1980s, is a public housing project with bold lines resembling a modern ocean liner. Breaking away from the stereotypes of social housing, the building offers spacious, bright, and flexible living spaces aimed at improving residents' quality of life. Nouvel used industrial materials such as steel and aluminum to give the structure a contemporary and durable aesthetic. The architecture of Nemausus 1 embodies a utopian vision, where social housing is synonymous with comfort and innovation. This project marked a turning point in public housing design in France.
programmes.subtitle: income housing project from the 1980s
programmes.title: Architectures

programmes.description: Lucian Freud, one of the most famous British painters of our time, is also one of the few twentieth-century artists to have portrayed himself so consistently in self-portraiture. His self-portraits provide a fascinating insight into both his personality and his development as a painter, from his first portrait in 1939 to his last. Through fascinating interviews with former models, friends and leading experts, this intensely captivating documentary reveals the work of a master who represents a compelling study of the dynamics of aging and the process of self-representation.
programmes.subtitle: Lucian Freud: A Self Portrait
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Discover the work of Matisse through the exhibitions at Tate Modern in London and MoMA in New York (2014) and enjoy the original performance of Royal Ballet star dancer Zenaida Yanowsky, who interprets the colors and dynamism of Matisse's painting to the jazz music of Courtney Pine. Punctuated by interviews with experts and rare archival footage of Matisse at work, this documentary will provide a special insight into the last chapter of the painter's career.
programmes.subtitle: Matisse From Moma and Tate Modern
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Narrated by Gillian Anderson, this episode of Exhibition on Screen follows the footsteps of French artists such as Renoir and Monet, the American Impressionist movement forged its own path. Painted over a period of 40 years, these paintings reveal the United States both as a nation and as a creative breeding ground. The history of this movement is closely linked to the love of gardens and the desire to preserve nature in a country undergoing rapid urbanization. This enchanting journey through workshops, gardens and famous sites in the USA, UK and France is a feast for the eyes.
programmes.subtitle: The Artist's garden: American Impressionism
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description:
Born in Aix-en-Provence in the South of France, Paul Cézanne (1839-1906) was a great French painter of the second half of the 19th century. Impressionist artist first, he is a initiator of the post-impressionnisme and the cubisme in his labour. In his still lifes and his “Bathers”, he is innovative in his geometric forms, which influenced the Cubist artists who came after him. He chose to paint the “Mont Saint Victoire” twenty times in his landscapes. Note the beautiful simplicity of “Apples and Oranges” composition or the quiet concentration of his “Card Players” both exposed at the Orsay museum.
Enjoy your visit!
programmes.subtitle: Paul Cézanne
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description: Discover or rediscover the masterpieces of the Dutch national museum Rijksmuseum with artists such as Rembrandt, Vermeer...
programmes.subtitle: Rijksmuseum
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description:
Actor and charmer Nigel Havers and his canny, deal-making chum (and ex-agent) Michael Whitehall explore the West Country. Travelling by Bentley and TVR, they’ll have £400 each and expert advice from Margie Cooper and James Braxton. 

But what will do best at the auction... Nigel’s old cockle bucket or Michael’s tambourine? 

Plus there’s a trip to see some Bristol Savages and bit of Georgian elegance with the story of ‘The King of Bath’.
programmes.subtitle: Michael Whitehall and Nigel Havers
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description: It was painted almost 600 years ago; the "Madonna at the Fountain" by Jan Van Eyck. Despite being a Charlotte’s favorite, she is reaching the limits of her ability. The minute details, the special use of oil paint and the slow-drying pigments play tricks on her. While the team is researching Van Eyck's complex oil painting technique, they are also travelling to Rome. In search for the deep blue ultramarine, in The Vatican they see the impact that Van Eyck had on his Italian contemporaries and lights a candle for Charlotte in the Santa Maria Maggiore.
programmes.subtitle: Madonna at the Fountain
programmes.title: Masterpiece

programmes.description: He is French, born in the suburbs of Paris to Beninese parents. But it is in Japan that King Houndekpinkou had a revelation and turned to an artistic career. He became a ceramist. The young artist evokes the earth within him with the magic of his hands and composes sculptural creations awakened by a vital spirit.
programmes.subtitle: King Houndekpinkou
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description: To mark the 500th anniversary of Raphael's death, a major exhibition has opened in Rome. Exhibition on Screen had exclusive access to this event, which brings together over 200 major works by this Renaissance master. The film explores the exhibition and sheds new light on the work of this often misunderstood or, on the contrary, idealized artist.
programmes.subtitle: Raphael Revealed
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Wilhelm Hansen was a visionary businessman who lived in Denmark in the 19th century. He was one of the few collectors to take an interest in the Impressionist painters, at a time when they were attacked and denigrated. The film takes us to Hansen's summer home on the outskirts of Copenhagen, and to the extraordinary exhibition of his collection at London's Royal Academy.
programmes.subtitle: The Danish Collector: Delacroix to Gauguin
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: He is one of the most controversial artists, yet one of the most influential. Picasso's collection contained mainly Renoirs. Matisse revered him. Monet too. Renoir was crucial to the creation of the Impressionist movement, before rejecting it altogether to embark on a radically different genre, with great success. The Barnes Collection in Philadelphia has more paintings by Renoir than any other gallery in the world, and it's here that we'll attempt to lift the veil on the remarkable story of this incredible artist.
programmes.subtitle: Renoir: Revered and Reviled
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description:
Two legends of British comedy, Ronni Ancona and Jan Ravens are joined on this Road Trip by antiquers Phil Serrell and James Braxton. Starting in the North Yorkshire town of Redcar they’ll head for auction in Stockport in Cheshire. 

Jan gets rather carried away and spends every single penny of her entire budget. While Ronni gets a kick out of a very kitsch glass boot. 

A quick detour sees Jan find out why Hartlepudlians thought a monkey was a Frenchman and Ronni is left open mouthed when Braxton takes off his clothes. Crikey!
programmes.subtitle: Ronni Ancona and Jan Ravens
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description:
Two favourite Blue Peter presenters Sarah Greene and Peter Duncan are in the company of Natasha Raskin and Catherine Southon as they hunt for antiques around Surrey, Hertfordshire and North West London. 

Peter detours to learn how hockey became a popular sport the world over while keen aviator Sarah sees how the Battle of Britain was won. 

An incredible haul of antiques, including chimney pots, Pinocchio and a pair of African fertility figures, go under the gavel at an auction in Tewkesbury, Gloucestershire.
programmes.subtitle: Sarah Greene and Peter Duncan
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description: Vermeer’s ‘Girl with the Pearl Earring’ was chosen by the public as the most beautiful painting in the Netherlands. It is also called the Mona Lisa of the low countries. The artwork has an incredibly beautiful light and almost inscrutable build-up of paint layers. What technique did Vermeer use to achieve this? The course of light and sharpness is unprecedented for its time. And is the pearl a pearl? The team will try to unravel these secrets by re-creating the painting with all the technology of today and knowledge of the past. Masterpiece faces many challenges in the search for Vermeer's secret.
programmes.subtitle: Girl with a Pearl Earring
programmes.title: Masterpiece

programmes.description: In 2019, the 500th anniversary of the death of Leonardo da Vinci was celebrated. To mark the occasion, the Louvre organised a major exhibition on the work of the most famous Renaissance painter. Echoing this event and based on the latest historiographical research, this documentary offers a new deciphering of the Tuscan master's paintings, revealing through them what painting represented for Leonardo: a philosophy, a total art in the service of understanding the world.
programmes.title: Decoding Da Vinci

programmes.description: During the 20th century, the fame of the ‘Mona Lisa’ spread, establishing itself as the most iconic and recognisable painting of all time. It has been exploited in every sphere of culture and advertising, to the extent that its status as a pop icon has almost overshadowed its artistic value and historical significance. But if we consider Leonardo’s achievements as a pioneering craftsman and the unprecedented qualities of this work, the ‘Mona Lisa’ truly marked a turning point in portraiture. A masterpiece that set new standards in its day and which, five hundred years later, has become the very symbol of art.
programmes.subtitle: Leonardo, The Mona Lisa
programmes.title: Masterpieces Unveiled

programmes.description: The story of “The Calling of Saint Matthew” begins on a hot summer day in Rome in 1600, the Jubilee Year. The entire Eternal City is a construction site: streets are full of scaffolding, dust clouds, loose cobblestones, the continuous banging of hammers and rasping of saws, carpenters with Lombard accents, errand boys shouting across the streets in Roman dialect, stevedores unloading barrels and crates from boats along the Tiber. The narrow streets in the town center are full of jostling tourists and monsignors rushing to get somewhere, and every once in a while the crowd parts to let a sedan chair or carriage of a cardinal through. Convent bells ring, droves of pilgrims mass along the routes connecting the old basilicas, reciting the rosary as they go. Not a day goes by without the opening of a new church, an oratory, or a chapel. Fascinated by this hubbub, dozens of artists from every nation roam the classical ruins and new palaces in the heat and dust (!) drawing everything they see.
programmes.subtitle: Caravaggio, Stories Of St. Matthew
programmes.title: Masterpieces Unveiled

programmes.description: Pablo Picasso is one of the world's greatest artists, and until his death in 1973, he was its most prolific. How did it all begin? After being ignored for too long, it's time to focus on the artist's early years and the upbringing that enabled him to achieve the extraordinary. Three cities played a key role: Malaga, Barcelona and Paris. Young Picasso traverses them and explores their influence on the artist, analyzing specific works from his early years.
programmes.subtitle: Young Picasso
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Discover or rediscover the masterpieces by Gustave Moreau (1826-1898) on display at the Musée d'Orsay, the Gustave Moreau Museum in Paris...
programmes.subtitle: Gustave Moreau
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description:
The man with the long greying beard who we find in this self-portrait is the painter Camille Pissarro (1830-1903). A keen follower of the Impressionist movement, the artist specialised in landscapes around Paris, often painted in winter, such as the “Chestnut Tress at Louveciennes” or the urban landscapes of Montmartre. Towards the end of his life, his painting technique changed and he turned towards Neo-Impressionism, for example in the “Seine River and Louvre Palace”.
Enjoy your visit!
programmes.subtitle: Camille Pissarro
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description: Between 1870 and 1914, the Menier factory in Noisiel was the largest chocolate factory in the world. But it was also, and above all, a pioneering factory in terms of architectural innovation. Its iron and then concrete architecture symbolized the company's power and modernity. Its three major buildings - the Saulnier Mill, the world's first all-steel structure, the Eiffel Hall and the Cathedral - tell the story of the golden age of industrial architecture.
programmes.subtitle: Menier Chocolate Factory
programmes.title: Architectures

programmes.description: Since the 1980s, street art has crept into cities and its artists are taking a growing place in urban space, but also in art collections. Installed in Lille, Jef Aerosol is part of the historical French Street Art with stencil option. His genre is the portrait, and he has long drawn on the world of music to express his passion. The artist is collected today by the greatest amateurs of Street Art.
programmes.subtitle: Jef Aerosol
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description: Nizhny Novgorod is the birthplace of Natalia Pankova. It is a closed city of the Soviet Union. The young Natalia knew very early that she wanted to become an artist, but not a Soviet artist, a free artist. In this episode, we will meet her in her studio.
programmes.subtitle: Natalia Pankova
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description:
Prog rocker Rick Wakeman and best mate Ian Lavender, loved as Pike from Dad’s Army, enjoy a jolly B-road ride around Norfolk. In the company of experts Raj Bisram and David Harper the two antique hunting celebrities scour the county for treasure to take to auction in Nottingham.

Rick also uncovers some hidden medieval graffiti in Norwich Cathedral while Ian detours to north Norfolk to see the world’s largest collection of model soldiers. 

But, will an wise old Japanese man help Ian win at auction?
programmes.subtitle: Rick Wakeman and Ian Lavender
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description: In this episode, meet the Photo Contest team in Lyon. The two candidates of the day, Mickael Gomes and Than Nguyen, will have one hour to take the best possible picture on the theme of gastronomy and those who make it. For this they will go to the Halles Paul Bocuse.
programmes.subtitle: Les Halles Bocuse
programmes.title: Photo Contest

programmes.description: In this episode, we will meet the artist Annette Messager. Her creations have been shaking up the contemporary scene for almost 50 years. She is one of the greatest French artists, awarded a Golden Lion at the Venice Biennale in 2005. She uses fabric and everyday objects to represent the intimate. But she also remains a committed artist. Installed in the popular suburbs of Paris, Annette Messager welcomes us in her workshop.
programmes.subtitle: Annette Messager
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description: Take an hour break to discover the work of a Spanish painter, Francisco de Goya. You will discover his labour with Lunch in the Countryside, The third of may 1808 or the Cannibals.

programmes.title: An hour with...

programmes.description: Exhibition on Screen takes us through the streets of Paris and then to the heart of a superb exhibition at Cambridge's Fitzwilliam Museum, whose impressive collection of Degas works is the most representative in Britain. Having benefited from exclusive access to a wide variety of rare works, the film tells the story of Degas' quest for perfection through experimentation.
programmes.subtitle: Degas: Passion for Perfection
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Discover some of the works of Georges Seurat realized during the end of the 19th century. These works are exhibited in Paris, Troyes or London.
programmes.subtitle: Georges Seurat

programmes.description:
In the second half of the 19th century, Edouard Manet (1832-1883) showed great originality in his painting of historic scenes and portraiture of well-known figures, such as the novelist Zola and the poet Mallarmé. Even if we cannot call him the first Impressionist, his leading role in the history of modern art must be emphasised. The scandals in 1863 caused by “The Luncheon on the Grass” or “Olympia” both exposed at the Orsay Museum effectively mark the beginning of modern painting.
Enjoy your visit!
programmes.subtitle: Edouard Manet
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description: At the Charlety Stadium, the architects have managed to reconcile opposites: the monumental grandeur of the stadium with that of the neighborhood, the life of a sports city with that of offices. Located at the Porte de Gentilly in Paris, squeezed between the ring road and the Boulevard des Maréchaux, the Charléty Stadium is bordered by the pavilions of the Cité universitaire, a cemetery and red brick HLM buildings. On this difficult eight-hectare site, marked by the fifty years of history of the old Sébastien-Charléty stadium, Henri Gaudin and his son Bruno have managed to implant the massive volume of a 20,000-seat covered stadium, as well as the sports facilities and offices commissioned by the City of Paris. In designing this large stadium with its gigantic ring shape, its elliptical stands and its aerial roof, the architects have been able to translate the energy that runs through the material and which is expressed in the sporting feat...
programmes.subtitle: Charlety, a stadium in the city
programmes.title: Architectures

programmes.description: Who was Frida Kahlo? Journey into the life of a true icon, discover her art and the truth behind her often turbulent life. The combination of interviews, commentary and a detailed exploration of Kahlo's art offers a treasure trove of color and a feast of vitality. This intimate, personal documentary provides privileged access to her works, and sheds light on her feverish creativity, resilience and unparalleled thirst for life.
programmes.subtitle: Frida Kahlo
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Every Rembrandt exhibition is eagerly awaited, but this exhibition organized by London's National Gallery and Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum was an unprecedented event. The documentary highlights the historic Rembrandt exhibition, while tracing his life. Rembrandt is one of the greatest artists who ever lived, and this deeply moving documentary seeks to explore the truth about the man behind the legend.
programmes.subtitle: Rembrandt at the National Gallery, London & Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: No artist captured the essence and charm of Venice better than Giovanni Antonio Canal, better known as Canaletto. This remarkable collection of over 200 paintings, drawings and etchings allows us to discover Canaletto's artistic talent, his contemporaries and the city he reproduced with genius. The film also opens the doors of two official royal residences, Buckingham Palace and Windsor Castle, to reveal more about the artist and Joseph Smith, the man who introduced Canaletto to Britain.
programmes.subtitle: Canaletto and the Art of Venice
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description:
Claude Monet is probably the best-known painter of the impressionist movement. Indeed, the term “impressionism” was derived from his painting “Impression Rising Sun” (1872). This exhibition retraces the great stages in Monet’s prolific career while dwelling on paintings of this master that cannot be ignored: the “Saint Lazare Station”, the “Poppies near Argenteuil”, the “Haystacks” and the “Rouen Cathedral” exposed all around the world in different museum such as the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston without forgetting his “Water-lilies” exposed at the Orangerie museum in Paris. 
Enjoy your visit!
programmes.subtitle: Monet
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description: On this July 14, 1906, day of the French national day, the tricolored flags float in the streets of Le Havre. Discover sumptuous works with landscapes of all kinds.
programmes.subtitle: Raoul Dufy
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description: Graffiti World is a short program dedicated to contemporary urban art around the world. Each episode explores a specific city, highlighting iconic works of street art. Local soundscape accompanies the images for an authentic, commentary-free immersion. The program showcases the creativity and diversity of artistic expression in public spaces. An invitation to discover the richness of graffiti as an art form in its own right.
programmes.title: Graffiti World

programmes.description:
TV chefs Aldo Zilli and Ching He-Huang do battle on this Road Trip around South Eastern England, aided by experts Natasha Raskin and Paul Laidlaw. 

Aldo plumps for a gold ring despite expert advice while Ching hopes antiques with an eastern origin will far well at auction in north London.

Aldo stops off to meet a 200 year old named ‘Jill’ to hear how she supplied locals with flour. And animal lover Ching learns how one man faced ridicule and ruin while trying to protect cattle in the 19th century.
programmes.subtitle: Huang and Aldo Zillix
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description:
Start by gathering several fascinating facts about Van Gogh’s life, which will then lead you to ask questions that uncover mysteries: What aspects of his life influenced his unique body of work—which is now worth hundreds of millions on the art market—and what ultimately drove him to commit an act of desperation? 
Discover Vincent van Gogh’s early years. From learning French and English to his very first art class, Brabant and its landscapes left an indelible mark on the young Vincent. Discover how Van Gogh made a sudden shift in his path, moving from the ministry and missionary work to a life devoted to art, aided in this by two influential men in his family. You’ll also begin to understand how his difficulties with his parents and scandals involving women would affect him.
What is it about the modest Protestant community in Nuenen that inspired Van Gogh to find his artistic voice, and why did he leave behind his extensive body of work when he moved away? This lecture explores how the.
programmes.subtitle: Dutch Master (In the Making)
programmes.title: Van Gogh: The Real Story

programmes.description:
In many ways, it is in Antwerp that Vincent begins the remarkable evolution that will ultimately make him one of the most important painters in modern art. Explore his journey at the Antwerp Academy, where he slowly sheds the darkness of Hague and begins to play with light and color. 
Did you know how much the Impressionist movement in Paris depended on Vincent’s brother, Theo? Find out the truth behind Theo’s enormous influence in promoting and establishing the movement and bringing together the Impressionist artists of the day, with scenes from Jean-Pierre Isbouts’ television drama Manet in Love. 
What would you do if a difficult relative dropped in without warning and announced they would be living with you from now on? Learn how Theo manages the situation when Vincent arrives in Paris, and revel in the way that Vincent inhales the wonderful new movements of Montmartre. By the 1880s, the Impressionists have slowly begun to drift apart after the deaths of Frédéric Bazille and Édouard.
programmes.subtitle: Vincent Discovers Colour
programmes.title: Van Gogh: The Real Story

programmes.description: In the suburbs of Paris, in Boulogne-Billancourt, there is an unusual place, « La ruche du Tag ». It's a space entirely dedicated to artists who are adept at Street Art. But before penetrating in this universe out of the common, it is necessary to leave on the step of the door our preconceived ideas on the graffitis and the Tags.
programmes.subtitle: The hive of Tag
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description:
Without Camille Pissarro, there is no Impressionist movement. He is rightfully known as the father of Impressionism.

It was a dramatic path that Pissarro followed, and throughout it all he wrote extensively to his family. It is through these intimate and revealing letters that this gripping film reveals Pissarro’s life and work.

Born in the West Indies, Pissarro found his passion in paint as a young man in Paris, and by the age of 43 had corralled a group of enthusiastic artists into a new collective. Their first show was scorned by the critics, but the group had acquired a new name: the Impressionists. For the next 40 years Pissarro was the driving force behind what has today become the world’s favourite artistic movement.

The Ashmolean Museum has a long tradition of excellence. As the UK’s first ever public museum (it opened its doors in May 1683) it houses a wonderfully rich collection, including the remarkable Pissarro archive. With exclusive access to most extensive archive of.
programmes.subtitle: Pissarro: Father of Impressionism
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Passionate about horticulture, Monet remains the undisputed master of garden painting in the history of art, but he was not alone. Artists such as Van Gogh, Bonnard, Picasso and Matisse used the garden as a strong theme in their work. These great artists, along with many other famous names, are brought together in an innovative exhibition from the Cleveland Museum of Art and the Royal Gallery of Arts in London. From the exhibition itself to the beauty of artists' gardens such as Monet's at Giverny, we take a journey to discover how the modern garden was used to explore radical and wondrous new ideas.
programmes.subtitle: Monet to Matisse
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Graffiti World is a short program dedicated to contemporary urban art around the world. Each episode explores a specific city, highlighting iconic works of street art. Local soundscape accompanies the images for an authentic, commentary-free immersion. The program showcases the creativity and diversity of artistic expression in public spaces. An invitation to discover the richness of graffiti as an art form in its own right.
programmes.title: Graffiti World

programmes.description: Born in Damascus, Syria, Ammar Abd Rabbo lived in Libya and Lebanon before moving to France at the age of 12. He has been working as a press photographer since 1990, and has signed more than sixty covers for well-known magazines. Ammar Abd Rabbo is not a war photographer, but has covered several conflicts, such as Iraq (2003), Lebanon (2006), Libya (2011), as well as several trips to Syria, in 2013 and 2014, to show the daily life and resistance of the inhabitants, rather than the military life.
programmes.subtitle: Ammar Abd Rabbo part 1
programmes.title: The decisive moment

programmes.description:
Pop Icon and actress Claire Grogan is reunited with fellow Glaswegian, Taggart actor Alex Norton as they battle it out in the search for profitable antiques. Anita Manning and Paul Laidlaw are on hand to lend their expertise. 

Anita and Alex find themselves on an Antiques ‘Boat’ Trip as they reminisce about childhood trips down the Clyde. While Claire and Paul see firsthand what Stirling castle would’ve looked like in the 16th century. 

The result of the auction in Ayr all rests on a naked lady.
programmes.subtitle: Alex Norton and Clare Grogan
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description:
Comedy legend Jennifer Saunders and best pal, top actress Patricia Potter take to the road on a humdinger of a trip. Joined by veteran antiquers Phillip Serrell and Mark Stacey they shop in Berkshire, Hampshire and Oxfordshire before heading for an auction in Greenwich, London. 
Jennifer and Phil detour to hear about Fred Karno, the man credited with inventing slapstick comedy. While Patricia and Mark learn how a surgeon from Reading used his incredible sense of smell to successfully treat soldiers injured in World War One.
And, Phil gets custard pied – what’s not to love?
programmes.subtitle: Jennifer Saunders and Patricia Potter
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description: Mondrian is one of the greatest innovators of Modern art. He started out as a landscape painter, but became world famous as a painter of abstract works. Mondrian tried to depict the world behind the visible world. He wanted to create "universal", harmonic art that would form the basis for a better world. His absolute masterpiece is ‘Victory Boogiewoogie’ the painting he worked on in New York until he died in 1944. Today it is known as the Night Watch of the twentieth century.
programmes.subtitle: Victory Boogiewoogie
programmes.title: Masterpiece

programmes.description: The image of the wealthy merchant from Lucca Giovanni Arnolfini shown together with his wife in the intimacy of their comfortable home in Bruges has always been considered the brilliant figurative proof of the commercial and artistic relations between Italy and Flanders in the 15th century. However, there has been a certain amount of doubtful attention devoted to the figures for some time; in fact, the hypothesis that one of the maximum masterpieces of portraiture of all times may not depict the Arnolfinis at all, but the van Eycks, is not entirely new. It had already been cautiously suggested by the Director of London’s National Gallery over a century and a half ago, when the painting was purchased by the great museum, but the idea was soon cast aside by the objections of specialists. Other doubts about the couple’s identity have cropped up a number of times, juggled back and forth amongst the abundant historic information on the painting, archival research, and allegorical theori.
programmes.subtitle: Van Eyck, The Arnolfini Portrait
programmes.title: Masterpieces Unveiled

programmes.description: This is Triptych of Earthly Delights: how did the great masterpiece by Jeroen Anthoniszoon van Aken, known as Hieronymus Bosch, come to be created, when was it painted, what was it used for, and what does it really represent? No one knows; for most of bosch’s works no documents or precise information about buyers exist. even the dating itself is complicated. Historians, archivists, and art critics have tried everything. A veil of mystery envelops his entire artistic production, giving rise to the most varied rumours but for now searching for clues in the local traditions, in the writings in latin, french, german and dutch, searching for possible iconographic precedents and parallels, peering into the murky mirror of magical rites and heresies, delving into alchemy treatises, and pulling out from the fog of history figures who had practically been forgotten. The search goes on, but for the time being we have no first-hand information. For almost all of bosch’s works, no conclusive d.
programmes.subtitle: Bosch, The Garden Of Earthly Delights
programmes.title: Masterpieces Unveiled

programmes.description: Lucian Freud, one of the most famous British painters of our time, is also one of the few twentieth-century artists to have portrayed himself so consistently in self-portraiture. His self-portraits provide a fascinating insight into both his personality and his development as a painter, from his first portrait in 1939 to his last. Through fascinating interviews with former models, friends and leading experts, this intensely captivating documentary reveals the work of a master who represents a compelling study of the dynamics of aging and the process of self-representation.
programmes.subtitle: Lucian Freud: A Self Portrait
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: "I envy the Japanese", wrote Van Gogh to his brother Theo. Thanks to the exhibition on which this film is based, at the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam, we understand why. Although Vincent van Gogh never visited Japan, it remains the country that had the greatest influence on him and his work. By visiting Japanese art galleries in Paris and creating his own image of Japan after extensive research, print collections and lengthy discussions with other artists, the discovery of Japanese art took van Gogh's career in an exciting new direction.
programmes.subtitle: Van Gogh and Japan
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Discover or rediscover Chaim Soutine's masterpieces, each one more surprising than the last.
programmes.subtitle: Chaïm Soutine
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description:
Founded at the end of the 19th century by the collector Richard Wallace, this private museum in London houses a truly beautiful collection of European paintings. Amongst others, one can admire “The Laughing Cavalier” by Frans Hals or Rembrandt’s portrait of “Titus, the Artist’s Son”. French painting of the 18th century, in Gallant and Rococo vein, is particularly well represented, including none other than the masterpiece of licentious painting: “The Swing” by Fragonard.
Enjoy your visit!
programmes.subtitle: The Wallace Collection
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description: Architect and urban planner Kenzo Tange is one of the most influential architects of his generation, having introduced Japan to the modern architecture discovered in the work of the masters. In 1987, he was the first Japanese to receive the Pritzker Prize, the world's highest distinction in architecture. To understand the true origins of the 2 Olympic gymnasiums built by Kenzo Tange for the 1964 Olympic Games, we have to go back to the defeat of Japan after the Second World War and the years that followed: Japan's occupation by the Americans, its absence from the international scene and its slow economic reconstruction. It's rare for a building to embody so many ambitions: those of an architect and a team of 25 young architects and urban planners, those of a city, those of a country determined to become a world power once again.
programmes.subtitle: Yoyogi Olympic Gymnasiums
programmes.title: Architectures

programmes.description: His white man is a symbol of Street Art in France. Jerome Mesnager was one of the spearheads of the emergence of this movement in the 1980s, in the wake of Ernest Pignon-Ernest and Gérard Zlotykamien. In France and around the world, the artist has multiplied his white man as a message.
programmes.subtitle: Jerome Mesnager
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description: In this episode we will meet the artist Norman Dilworth. His working method is through play and experimentation. He assembles elements in a sequential order, or elements that already have a sequential relationship. Using primitive means and simple systems, he creates structures that express growth in a principle of natural development.
programmes.subtitle: Norman Dilworth
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description:
Actor and charmer Nigel Havers and his canny, deal-making chum (and ex-agent) Michael Whitehall explore the West Country. Travelling by Bentley and TVR, they’ll have £400 each and expert advice from Margie Cooper and James Braxton. 

But what will do best at the auction... Nigel’s old cockle bucket or Michael’s tambourine? 

Plus there’s a trip to see some Bristol Savages and bit of Georgian elegance with the story of ‘The King of Bath’.
programmes.subtitle: Michael Whitehall and Nigel Havers
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description: Today, we go to Marseille where two new candidates will compete. Juan Bosco Gomez Herrera and Lilian Heymans will have one hour to take the best possible photograph on the imposed theme of the sea.
programmes.subtitle: Marseille, the sea
programmes.title: Photo Contest

programmes.description: In the western suburbs of Paris, we are going to discover the studio of the artist Jérôme Zonder. For more than 10 years, the artist has been developing a virtuoso work focused on drawing. Made with charcoal or graphite, his dark and often very realistic works arouse both admiration and fear. Powerful and complex, Jérôme Zonder's art captivates by its technical prowess and questions our relationship to violence.
programmes.subtitle: Jérôme Zonder
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description: Take an hour break to discover the work of a French painter, Édouard Vuillard. You will discover his labour with Sleep, The Piano or Portrait de madame Henri Vaquez.
programmes.subtitle: Édouard Vuillard
programmes.title: An hour with...

programmes.description: Take an hour break to discover the work of an Italian painter, Titien. You will discover his labour with Pastoral concert, The resurrection of Christ or Venus with organist.
programmes.subtitle: Titien
programmes.title: An hour with...

programmes.description: Pablo Picasso is one of the world's greatest artists, and until his death in 1973, he was its most prolific. How did it all begin? After being ignored for too long, it's time to focus on the artist's early years and the upbringing that enabled him to achieve the extraordinary. Three cities played a key role: Malaga, Barcelona and Paris. Young Picasso traverses them and explores their influence on the artist, analyzing specific works from his early years.
programmes.subtitle: Young Picasso
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Discover the secrets of this talented artist's masterpieces. Géricault's first work was exhibited to the public at the 1812 Salon in Paris. Géricault once again demonstrates his incredible mastery of portraits in which the search for realism does not alter the psychological dimension of the model, but on the contrary sublimates it.
programmes.subtitle: Théodore Géricault
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description:
Born in Aix-en-Provence in the South of France, Paul Cézanne (1839-1906) was a great French painter of the second half of the 19th century. Impressionist artist first, he is a initiator of the post-impressionnisme and the cubisme in his labour. In his still lifes and his “Bathers”, he is innovative in his geometric forms, which influenced the Cubist artists who came after him. He chose to paint the “Mont Saint Victoire” twenty times in his landscapes. Note the beautiful simplicity of “Apples and Oranges” composition or the quiet concentration of his “Card Players” both exposed at the Orsay museum.
Enjoy your visit!
programmes.subtitle: Paul Cézanne
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description:
Raphael Federici (street artist), Marine Goodmorning (illustrator), Luca Fiore (cartoonist) and Harry Boudchicha (drawing teacher) reveal their best drawing techniques. Each episode focuses on a specific subject:
movement, oil painting, shadows, hair... For the first 10 minutes, each artist gives a theoretical lesson illustrated by sketches. Then they each start working on their creation. Finally, they end with a debrief, comparing
and explaining their techniques.
programmes.subtitle: Calligraphy
programmes.title: Sketchbook

programmes.description: In 64 episodes, fun and educational, you will know how to draw an airplane, a fireman, a haunted mansion, a soccer player, a sunset, a lion, the Eiffel Tower, seashells, a fairy... Our master draftsman Gia-Haï Phan will show you the basics of a successful drawing: proportions, perspectives, values, contrasts, volumes, blending, everything is covered.
programmes.title: Little Sketches

programmes.description: André Godin, inspired by Charles Fourier's phalanstères, envisioned a palatial communal living space for his workers. From 1860 to 1968, the Guise Familistère, a community built for 1800 inhabitants by the great Fourierist industrialist Jean-Baptiste-André Godin (1817-1889), served as the stage for a social experiment that remained unique in its audacity, scale, and duration. The invention of a "unitary" architecture and urban planning is one of the original and pioneering aspects of the Familistère adventure. This "Social Palace" constituted a true utopia in action, which today once again arouses the interest of historians, sociologists, economists, urban planners, and architects.
programmes.subtitle: The Guise familistère, a radiant city
programmes.title: Architectures

programmes.description: Wilhelm Hansen was a visionary businessman who lived in Denmark in the 19th century. He was one of the few collectors to take an interest in the Impressionist painters, at a time when they were attacked and denigrated. The film takes us to Hansen's summer home on the outskirts of Copenhagen, and to the extraordinary exhibition of his collection at London's Royal Academy.
programmes.subtitle: The Danish Collector: Delacroix to Gauguin
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: After a two-year touring exhibition, in 2015 Girl with a Pearl Earring returned to the Mauritshuis Museum in The Hague. At 350 years old, the eternal Girl has always retained her aura of mystery and charm. The proof is in the number of curious onlookers (1.2 million) who flocked to catch a glimpse of her during her stay in Japan. The documentary seeks to uncover the many enigmas surrounding this extraordinary painting and its mysterious creator - Vermeer. Who was this girl? Why and how did Vermeer paint this picture? Come and travel back in time to discover Johannes Vermeer, visit the charming museum in The Hague and answer all these questions.
programmes.subtitle: Girl with a Pearl Earring
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: David Hockney, generally considered one of Britain's most popular artists, has enjoyed worldwide success throughout his life, with exhibitions in London, New York, Paris and elsewhere attracting millions of visitors. This film reveals intimate, previously unseen interviews and focuses on two successful exhibitions that took place in 2012 and 2016 at the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
programmes.subtitle: David Hockney at the Royal Academy of Arts
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description:
With his considerable production of more than 6,000 works, Auguste Renoir took part in the emergence of the impressionist movement even if he were to distance himself from it later to assert a more personal style. This visit begins with his most famous masterpiece, the “Ball at the Moulin de la Galette”. You will also rediscover the “Dance in the City” and the “Piano Lesson” exposed at the Joslyn art museum as well as “Claude Renoir in Clown Costume”, a portrait of his son who was later to become one of France’s greatest film directors exposed at the Orangerie Museum in France 
Enjoy your visit!
programmes.subtitle: Renoir
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description: In this programme, you will find some of the masterpieces exhibited in this Galleries of Scotland.
programmes.subtitle: National Galleries of Scotland
programmes.title: Within the frame

programmes.description: Graffiti World is a short program dedicated to contemporary urban art around the world. Each episode explores a specific city, highlighting iconic works of street art. Local soundscape accompanies the images for an authentic, commentary-free immersion. The program showcases the creativity and diversity of artistic expression in public spaces. An invitation to discover the richness of graffiti as an art form in its own right.
programmes.title: Graffiti World

programmes.description:
Two legends of British comedy, Ronni Ancona and Jan Ravens are joined on this Road Trip by antiquers Phil Serrell and James Braxton. Starting in the North Yorkshire town of Redcar they’ll head for auction in Stockport in Cheshire. 

Jan gets rather carried away and spends every single penny of her entire budget. While Ronni gets a kick out of a very kitsch glass boot. 

A quick detour sees Jan find out why Hartlepudlians thought a monkey was a Frenchman and Ronni is left open mouthed when Braxton takes off his clothes. Crikey!
programmes.subtitle: Ronni Ancona and Jan Ravens
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description: This is Triptych of Earthly Delights: how did the great masterpiece by Jeroen Anthoniszoon van Aken, known as Hieronymus Bosch, come to be created, when was it painted, what was it used for, and what does it really represent? No one knows; for most of bosch’s works no documents or precise information about buyers exist. even the dating itself is complicated. Historians, archivists, and art critics have tried everything. A veil of mystery envelops his entire artistic production, giving rise to the most varied rumours but for now searching for clues in the local traditions, in the writings in latin, french, german and dutch, searching for possible iconographic precedents and parallels, peering into the murky mirror of magical rites and heresies, delving into alchemy treatises, and pulling out from the fog of history figures who had practically been forgotten. The search goes on, but for the time being we have no first-hand information. For almost all of bosch’s works, no conclusive d.
programmes.subtitle: Bosch, The Garden Of Earthly Delights
programmes.title: Masterpieces Unveiled

programmes.description: The image of the wealthy merchant from Lucca Giovanni Arnolfini shown together with his wife in the intimacy of their comfortable home in Bruges has always been considered the brilliant figurative proof of the commercial and artistic relations between Italy and Flanders in the 15th century. However, there has been a certain amount of doubtful attention devoted to the figures for some time; in fact, the hypothesis that one of the maximum masterpieces of portraiture of all times may not depict the Arnolfinis at all, but the van Eycks, is not entirely new. It had already been cautiously suggested by the Director of London’s National Gallery over a century and a half ago, when the painting was purchased by the great museum, but the idea was soon cast aside by the objections of specialists. Other doubts about the couple’s identity have cropped up a number of times, juggled back and forth amongst the abundant historic information on the painting, archival research, and allegorical theori.
programmes.subtitle: Van Eyck, The Arnolfini Portrait
programmes.title: Masterpieces Unveiled

programmes.description: John Singer Sargent is known as the greatest portrait artist of his era. What made his ‘swagger’ portraits remarkable was his power over his sitters, what they wore and how they were presented to the audience. Through interviews with curators, contemporary fashionistas and style influencers, Exhibition on Screen’s film will examine how Sargent’s unique practice has influenced modern art, culture and fashion.
programmes.subtitle: John Singer Sargent: Fashion and Swagger
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Lionel Estève has been living in the Molenbeek district of Brussels for nearly 20 years. It is here that he has set up his studio, an ideal space to practice his art, as well as to highlight the cheerfulness of the colors he uses and the softness of nature that he transmits in his work.
programmes.subtitle: Lionel Estève
programmes.title: Artist's Workshop

programmes.description:
Hopper’s work is the most recognisable art in America – popular, praised, and mysterious. Countless painters, photographers, filmmakers and musicians have been influenced by his art – but who was he, and how did a struggling illustrator create such a bounty of notable work?
This new film takes a deep look into Hopper’s art, his life, and his relationships. From his early career as an illustrator; his wife giving up her own promising art career to be his manager; his critical and commercial acclaim; and in his own words – this film explores the enigmatic personality behind the brush….
programmes.subtitle: Story
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: Multi-award-winning director Phil Grabsky takes a fresh look at arguably the world's most beloved artist, using the words of the painter himself. I, Claude Monet reveals new facets of the man who gave birth to the Impressionist movement with one painting, and who was certainly one of the most influential and renowned painters of the 19th and early 20th centuries. Shot on location across Europe, I, Claude Monet is an unprecedented, intimate film exploration of some of Western art's most beloved cult settings.
programmes.subtitle: I, Claude Monet
programmes.title: Exhibition on Screen

programmes.description: In this episode, we meet Ammar Abd Rabbo, press photographer. He says of his work, that he likes to write thanks to photos. He does not define himself as a war reporter but rather as a generalist reporter. He likes to diversify: one day he wants to photograph the Cannes Film Festival, another day he wants to photograph a political event...
programmes.subtitle: Ammar Abd Rabbo part 2
programmes.title: The decisive moment

programmes.description:
Top presenting pals Nicki Chapman and Jules Hudson escape to the country to find antiques with Natasha Raskin and Phillip Serrell. It becomes girls versus boys, both teams with £400 in their pockets. Kicking off from Wormsley in Herefordshire they Road Trip into Wales and Oxfordshire, before finally finishing in North Finchley, in London for an auction.

Along the way the girls meet a clog maker who carves shoes by hand. While the boys head to the Herefordshire Light Infantry Museum to hear about the regiment’s involvement at Gallipoli.
programmes.subtitle: Nicki Chapman and Jules Hudson
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description:
Legends of stage and screen, Charles Dance and Geraldine James join antiques experts Natasha Raskin and Will Axon on this Road Trip romp around Wiltshire. 
Charles finds a pair of Edwardian silver vases he hopes will prove profitable at an auction in Essex. Geraldine, however, bumps into a chap in the street with a 19th Century French Empire secretaire. It costs her a small fortune – will the gamble pay off? 
A diversion from the shops sees Charles end up in the cockpit of a very old helicopter while Geraldine learns how a small part of Swindon dating back 170 years influenced the creation of the modern NHS.
programmes.subtitle: Charles Dance and Geraldine James
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description: Rembrandt: without a doubt the greatest painter in the Netherlands. Admired all over the world, especially for his play with light and dark. He was a Dutch celebrity avant la lettre, the superstar of the Golden Age ... A master of portraying human emotions, especially when it comes to his self-portraits. Technical virtuoso, but also ruthlessly honest. Rembrant painted his first self-portrait when he was 22. A small, but technically very refined work: "Self-portrait at an early age." Is the team able to unravel some of the secrets of Rembrandt's shadow play?
programmes.subtitle: Self Portrait
programmes.title: Masterpiece

programmes.description:
A celebrity couple Road Trip – award winning journalists John Stapleton and Lynn Faulds Wood.
 
Joining them on this jolly jaunt are Thomas Plant and Margie Cooper. With £400 in their pockets the teams kick off in Wrightington, Lancashire and head to Stockport for auction. 

Lynn and Thomas find themselves literally knee deep in antiques while hunting for old biscuit tins while Margie tries to convince John some rare lamps will make a profit. 

Also John learns how an American revolutionised British public transport and Lynn sees why snakes are milked in Liverpool.
programmes.subtitle: Lynne Faulds Wood and John Stapleton
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description:
TV chefs Aldo Zilli and Ching He-Huang do battle on this Road Trip around South Eastern England, aided by experts Natasha Raskin and Paul Laidlaw. 

Aldo plumps for a gold ring despite expert advice while Ching hopes antiques with an eastern origin will far well at auction in north London.

Aldo stops off to meet a 200 year old named ‘Jill’ to hear how she supplied locals with flour. And animal lover Ching learns how one man faced ridicule and ruin while trying to protect cattle in the 19th century.
programmes.subtitle: Huang and Aldo Zillix
programmes.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip

programmes.description: Acest tur aerian spectaculos dezvăluie Insulele Spaniei, așa cum nu au mai fost văzute până acum. Camerele dronelor planează deasupra Insulelor Canare, dezvăluind cel mai important observator astronomic din Europa și o podgorie unică, ce prosperă la umbra unui vulcan. Vom explora emblematica catedrala gotică a Insulelor Baleare, înălțându-se deasupra portului din Palma, Mallorca, și vom vizita festivalul focului.
programmes.subtitle: Insulele Spaniei
programmes.title: Europa văzută de sus

programmes.description: Arheologii investighează misterul mormântului mic și simplu al lui Tutankhamon. Domnia sa a fost modelată de tatăl acestuia, un faraon care a condus cea mai mare revoluție din istoria religioasă a Egiptului. Să fi fost această revoluție, împreună cu intriga politică ce a urmat, cauza exilării lui Tutankhamon după moarte într-un mormânt nepotrivit unui faraon ?
programmes.subtitle: Misterul lui Tutankhamon
programmes.title: Comori pierdute ale Egiptului

programmes.subtitle: Răstignirea
programmes.title: Enigme vechi

programmes.description: Vedeta „Brooklyn Nine-Nine” Terry Crews i se alătură lui Bear Grylls într-o călătorie epică pe terenul dificil al Islandei. Aventura lor începe cu o plimbare cu heli-skiul în munți, unde trebuie să coboare pe o pantă vulcanică fără să declanșeze o avalanșă mortală de pietre. Supraviețuirea este numele jocului pentru acest fost jucător de fotbal profesionist, devenit actor: de la încercarea de traversare a apelor violente, înghețate, fără să se înece și până la găsirea unui adăpost cald pentru a evita hipotermia. Însă nimic nu îl poate pregăti pe Terry pentru săritura dintr-un avion de la 3,6 km!
programmes.subtitle: Terry Crews în Islanda
programmes.title: Vedete în sălbăticie, cu Bear Grylls

programmes.description: Trei dezastre reale investigate medico-legal, analizate și recreate în detalii uimitoare, pe baza expertizei și a tuturor dovezilor disponibile. Cum a fost sfâșiată în bucăți naveta Columbia la reintrarea în atmosferă? De ce au murit atât de mulți oameni în cel mai grav accident de tren de mare viteză, la Eschede, în Germania? Cum a devenit un turn înalt din beton din Londra, numit Grenfell Tower, un infern care a ucis 72 de oameni?
programmes.subtitle: Columbia, trenul Eschede și turnul Grenfell
programmes.title: Dezastre investigate

programmes.description: Ciudat, anormal și extraordinar sunt atributele unei zile ”tipice” la clinica doctorului Pol, dar săptămâna aceasta lucrurile o iau razna de-a binelea! Printre pacienți se numără un cangur pitic cu o protuberanță bizară, o vacă cu un vițel mutant și o căpriță extrem de mică!
programmes.subtitle: Cazuri bizare
programmes.title: Doctor Pol

programmes.description: O nouă săptămână agitată în Michigan! De la atacuri ale animalelor la bovine care evadează și oi ce nu se lasă prinse cu una cu două, veterinarii sunt solicitați continuu și nu au timp de pierdut.
programmes.subtitle: Oi și alte cele
programmes.title: Doctor Pol

programmes.description: Echipa de veterinari se îndreaptă către ferma campionului NBA Dwight Howard Jr. unde ajută în mai multe probleme legate de animale. Mai târziu, dr. Ferguson se ocupă de un câine și un cobai, în timp ce dr. Hodges încearcă să salveze un șarpe sălbatic cu răni mortale. Între timp, o șopârlă nu se simte deloc bine, iar un cățel face o supradoză cu medicamentele pentru durere ale proprietarului său.
programmes.subtitle: veterinari la țară : O șopârlă încercată
programmes.title: Salvatorii animalelor

programmes.description: Dr. Hodges cheamă un neașteptat erou ca să ajute la salvarea unui cățeluș bolnav, pe nume Titan. Dr. Ferguson tratează un cerb orb și își pune ingeniozitatea la încercare când el și dr. Hodges ajută o pasăre nandu rănită. Apoi, este investigat misterul unei capre pitice nigeriene, amuzantul dihor Niffler vine la clinică pentru o problemă nu atât de amuzantă la o lăbuță, iar Bailey, iepurașul, dezvăluie o surpriză șocantă!
programmes.subtitle: veterinari la țară : Salvatorul lui Titan
programmes.title: Salvatorii animalelor

programmes.description: Îndreptându-se către o fermă de reni când turma este în perioada de împerechere, dr. Oakley operează un ren cu pleoapa ruptă. Apoi, veterinarii trebuie să mâne într-un loc sigur câțiva reni scăpați. Înapoi la clinică, echipa operează un câine și ajută o pisică cu blana foarte încâlcită.
programmes.subtitle: Ren fugar
programmes.title: Veterinar în Yukon

programmes.description: O cobră îşi împroaşcă victima cu venin. Un mamba stă bine ascuns, apoi atacă brusc. Un cuib de şobolani provoacă agitaţie mare.

programmes.subtitle: Atitudine colțoasă

programmes.description: Documentarul debutează cu un preview dinamic a a ceea ce urmează să ofere seria – și anume povestea din culise a unei echipe de elită care construiește un sistem de metrou revoluționar, complet automatizat, în valoare de 50 de miliarde de dolari. Este, de departe, cea mai mare și mai avansată linie feroviară nouă inaugurată oriunde pe planetă în 2019. O scenă dramatică, în care personajele principale se confruntă cu o criză, dă startul acțiunii. Membrii echipei își exprimă apoi, într-un montaj de opinii, motivele pentru care acest megaproiect este atât de remarcabil și cum va rivaliza cu cele mai bune sisteme din lume. Amploarea uriașă a lucrărilor care urmează este copleșitoare, lucru evidențiat clar într-o prezentare de ansamblu. O secvență CGI spectaculoasă ne arată ce trebuie realizat: tuneluri apar sub Gara Centrală, îndreptându-se spre nord, traversând un adevărat câmp minat de obstacole subterane și stații noi, înainte de a trece pe sub port și de a continua spre nord-vest. Pe traseu apar stații noi, până la un imens depou de întreținere a trenurilor și un centru de comandă, la Rouse Hill, traversând o zonă inundabilă pe un viaduct numit Skytrain. Din Gara Centrală, alte tuneluri se întind spre sud, străbătând orașul până la Bankstown. O altă linie nouă pornește spre Parramatta, cu o conexiune suplimentară către un aeroport nou. Membrii echipei ne spun cât de conștienți sunt de dimensiunea colosală a sarcinii lor și de faptul că au la dispoziție doar câțiva ani pentru a construi totul.
programmes.subtitle: În acțiune
programmes.title: Metrou inovator

programmes.description: Echipa pornește în următoarea provocare uriașă, forând sub un oraș vechi de 230 de ani, unde îi așteaptă obstacole de tot felul. Două noi mașini de forat tuneluri, 5 și 6, pleacă din suburbia Marrickville din Sydney, forând spre nord, către inima districtului central de afaceri. Destinația finală este o stație de pe malul apei, la Barangaroo, aflată la 10 kilometri distanță. Urmărim echipa în timp ce se confruntă cu numeroase dificultăți, săpând printr-un adevărat câmp minat de infrastructură existentă: fundațiile și subsolurile zgârie-norilor, canale de scurgere, un cimitir și tuneluri feroviare deja existente. În mai multe puncte, mașinile de forat tuneluri trebuie să „treacă prin urechea acului”, cu foarte puțin spațiu de manevră. La suprafață, excavarea unor cantități uriașe de pământ pe străzi înguste și aglomerate ale orașului ridică alte provocări.

Intrând într-o lume a lăcomiei și cruzimii profunde, Mariana descoperă cum cercuri infracționale internaționale vizează americanii în vârstă pentru a-i ademeni în fraude cu moșteniri și îi conving să devină cărăruși de droguri.

programmes.description: Simpla trimitere a oamenilor în spațiu este o misiune extrem de riscantă. Aflați într-o rachetă, astronauții trebuie să supraviețuiască exploziei controlate care lansează nava dincolo de atmosferă și forțelor de frecare înspăimântătoare din timpul reintrării. Este un mediu neiertător, în care erori minore au provocat catastrofe mortale și costisitoare. Pentru a-și pregăti pentru viitor noua capsulă pentru spațiul profund, Orion, inginerii NASA trebuie să analizeze în detaliu fiecare dezastru din trecut. De la exploziile devastatoare ale navetelor spațiale până la tragediile Apollo și Soyuz, eșecurile de ieri reprezintă lecții esențiale. Dezvoltarea unor noi costume de supraviețuire, îmbunătățirea sistemelor de evacuare și inovarea unor materiale noi fac călătoria în spațiu mai sigură ca niciodată.

programmes.description: În Midyat, Turcia, arheologii descoperă vastul oraș subteran Matiate, întins pe tuneluri și încăperi săpate acum mii de ani. Dovezile unor biserici, sinagogi și monede romane sugerează că a fost cândva un refugiu pentru cei care fugeau de persecuții religioase. În Royston, Anglia, muncitorii dau peste o cameră misterioasă săpată în cretă, plină de sculpturi religioase complexe. Sub Orvieto, Italia, săpăturile pentru o pivniță de vin scot la iveală Cavità 254, un impresionant complex subteran etrusc. Cândva carieră sau sistem de apă, umplerea sa intenționată cu ceramică și oase sugerează practici ritualice sau simbolice de înmormântare. În final, în Abarkuh, Iran, arheologii cartografiază o vastă rețea de tuneluri subterane, probabil parte a unui vechi sistem de irigații qanat, exemplu al ingeniozității persane, folosit pentru a supraviețui secetei, războiului și căldurii deșertului.
programmes.subtitle: Orașe subterane și camere secrete
programmes.title: Lumi ascunse sub orașe

programmes.description: De-a lungul istoriei, vindecarea a luat numeroase forme surprinzătoare. În Europa medievală, oamenii apelau la bărbieri-chirurgi, care tundeau părul și efectuau intervenții chirurgicale în mijlocul epidemiilor de ciumă și al conflictelor, punând bazele medicinei profesioniste. În Anglia elisabetană, medicii instruiți în astrologie priveau către cer pentru răspunsuri, crezând că mișcările planetelor dețineau cheia diagnosticului și a vindecării. Cu secole înainte, în India Antică, un inovator remarcabil a sfidat tabuurile sociale pentru a dezvolta chirurgia, a crea instrumente specializate și a extinde cunoștințele anatomice prin principiile ayurvedice. De la îngrijirea răniților pe câmpul de luptă la medicina ghidată de stele și chirurgia revoluționară, aceste practici dezvăluie bazele diverse ale științei medicale.
programmes.subtitle: Mistere dezvăluite: Frizeri, astrologi și medicina indiană antică
programmes.title: Medicina Antică

programmes.description: 1491, Irlanda. Un tânăr pretinde a fi Richard, Duce de York, unul dintre prinții pierduți în Turnul Londrei. Susținut de puterile europene, acesta reprezintă o amenințare gravă pentru regele Henric al VII-lea al Angliei. Suzannah Lipscomb și Dan Snow reexaminează dovezile care îl înconjoară pe unul dintre cei mai convingători pretendenți la tron ​​din istorie. A fost acesta, de fapt, conducătorul de drept al Angliei?
programmes.subtitle: Putere, Trădare și execuții: Perkin Warbeck și Prinții Turnului
programmes.title: Dinastia Tudorilor

programmes.description: După ce a susținut că a primit de la Iisus Hristos o misiune divină, Sun Myung Moon a sfidat doctrina religioasă tradițională și a fondat Biserica Unificării, o mișcare globală care a atras milioane de adepți. Însă, pe măsură ce influența organizației a crescut, au apărut și numeroase acuzații. Cine a fost acest autoproclamat trimis al lui Dumnezeu și care au fost adevăratele sale motive? După ce a prezis cu exactitate asasinarea președintelui John F. Kennedy, viscolul devastator din Chicago din 1967 și uciderea unei moștenitoare bogate, Irene Hughes a fost supranumită „cel mai precis medium al Americii”. În Roma Antică, generalul Publius Claudius Pulcher a ignorat prevestirile transmise de găinile sacre folosite în ritualurile de divinație și și-a găsit sfârșitul. Povestea sa rămâne un avertisment despre consecințele sfidării voinței zeilor.
programmes.subtitle: Regatul cultelor, Moartea președintelui, Găini sacre
programmes.title: Decodificarea profețiilor istorice

programmes.description: În fiecare an, în mijlocul iernii, în timpul celui mai secetos sezon, râul Okavango inundă Kalahari, transformând deșertul într-un Eden. Fiți martorii acestui spectacol natural extraordinar. Pe măsură ce apele umplu delta, elefanții se grăbesc să traverseze deșertul, leii se luptă pentru teritoriu, iar fauna sălbatică se trezește în ritmul curentului. Acest miracol este unul trecător. De la lumile subacvatice de sub rădăcinile de papirus la ambuscadele leilor, urmăriți râul în timp ce oferă hrană și apoi o ia înapoi, pe măsură ce apa se retrage.

programmes.description: A doua parte a serialului începe odată cu plecarea zebrelor. În timp ce prima parte era în nuanțe de maro și galben, aceasta este colorată în verde. Ploile vin, peisajul se schimbă și se apropie vremuri dificile. Nivelul râurilor în creștere inundă zona, iar curenții sunt periculoși. Poate fi paradisul, dar este un paradis dur. Când ploile se potolesc, ne întoarcem la unul dintre personajele din primul episod, o femelă serval al cărei bârlog a fost inundat, dar aceasta și puiul ei au supraviețuit, un adevărat miracol în aceste condiții.

programmes.description: Știm că rechinii-taur înoată în amonte pe fluvii și că vânează în mări. Însă nu i-am văzut niciodată ca acum. Îi observăm atacând și devorând alți rechini. Îi urmărim la vânătoare în adâncuri. Îi vedem ajungând în ape dulci către locurile de reproducere. Îi surprindem din drone atacând bancuri de pești sau în încleștări cu hipopotami și crocodili.
programmes.subtitle: taur
programmes.title: Secretele rechinului-taur

programmes.description: Urmărim călătoria captivantă a unui tânăr jaguar, pornind în cea mai importantă misiune din viața lui, găsirea propriului regat. Pentru a-și dovedi valoarea și a-și revendica tronul, trebuie să străbată unele dintre cele mai sălbatice peisaje de pe planetă, fiecare populat cu vietăți unice.
programmes.subtitle: simbolul Guyanei: Jaguarul: simbolul Guyanei
programmes.title: Jaguarul

programmes.description: Narat de faimoasa actriță Angela Bassett de la Hollywood și realizat de producătorii câștigători ai premilor Emmy cu ”Planet Earth II”, ”Blue Planet” și ”Hostile Planet”, prin acest documentar o urmărim pe Malika în timp ce se confruntă cu greutățile trecerii de la copilărie la maturitate. Leoaica rebuie să învețe să vâneze și să ajute la protejarea familiei de intrușii mortali.
programmes.subtitle: Leoaica regină : Pericol iminent
programmes.title: Malika

programmes.description: În fiecare an, în mijlocul iernii, în timpul celui mai secetos sezon, râul Okavango inundă Kalahari, transformând deșertul într-un Eden. Fiți martorii acestui spectacol natural extraordinar. Pe măsură ce apele umplu delta, elefanții se grăbesc să traverseze deșertul, leii se luptă pentru teritoriu, iar fauna sălbatică se trezește în ritmul curentului. Acest miracol este unul trecător. De la lumile subacvatice de sub rădăcinile de papirus la ambuscadele leilor, urmăriți râul în timp ce oferă hrană și apoi o ia înapoi, pe măsură ce apa se retrage.
programmes.subtitle: Paradis
programmes.title: Râul-fantomă al Africii

programmes.description: În timpul sezonului uscat, râul Boteti este un loc de odihnă prețios pentru zeci de mii de animale. Apele sale le permit să supraviețuiască migrației anuale dintre Delta Okavango și pajiștile Makgadikgadi. Când răul dispare brusc, toată viața de aici trebuie să se adapteze la realitățile unei secete de mai mulți ani.
programmes.subtitle: Linia de salvare
programmes.title: Râul-fantomă al Africii

programmes.description: La gura de vărsare a râului Boteti, albia secată a unui fost lac se întinde la infinit. Deși peisajul este arid și pustiu, dintr-o dată, ca prin magie, erbivorele din Kalahari încep să se adune aici. Dar oare norii de ploaie, semnalizați de instinctele lor, vor sosi în ordine, transformând peste noapte deșertul într-un paradis verde? Vor deveni Câmpiile Nxai un loc de odihnă revigorant și dătător de viață pentru nomazii din Kalahari sau vor muri cu toții în praf când ploile vor înceta?
programmes.subtitle: Moartea în praf
programmes.title: Râul-fantomă al Africii

programmes.description: Prima parte a seriei noastre începe cu turme de gnu care traversează râul și dispar în depărtare. Lasă în urmă praf și sute, poate mii, de alte animale care nu pot sau nu vor să plece. Sunt legate de teritoriile lor, delimitate de granițe invizibile. În povestea noastră, este vorba despre aceste animale. Aflăm ce se întâmplă în regiunea Mara între septembrie și iulie, nouă luni fără antilopele gnu.
programmes.subtitle: renașterea: Începutul
programmes.title: Mara

programmes.description: A doua parte a serialului începe odată cu plecarea zebrelor. În timp ce prima parte era în nuanțe de maro și galben, aceasta este colorată în verde. Ploile vin, peisajul se schimbă și se apropie vremuri dificile. Nivelul râurilor în creștere inundă zona, iar curenții sunt periculoși. Poate fi paradisul, dar este un paradis dur. Când ploile se potolesc, ne întoarcem la unul dintre personajele din primul episod, o femelă serval al cărei bârlog a fost inundat, dar aceasta și puiul ei au supraviețuit, un adevărat miracol în aceste condiții.
programmes.subtitle: renașterea: Trezirea
programmes.title: Mara

programmes.description: Veterinarii de la clinică reușesc să facă zilnic adevărate minuni. Dr. Brenda și dr. Lisa tratează o varietate de răni ale picioarelor, inclusiv un sheltie cu degetele rupte. Dr. Pol examinează un câine masiv cu probleme digestive și un iepure rănit, iar dr. Nicole este ocupată cu un cocoș și o pisică.
programmes.subtitle: Urme false
programmes.title: Doctor Pol

programmes.description: Când vine vorba de accidentări ciudate, veterinarii noștri au văzut totul. Astăzi, ochiul rănit al unei pisici ascunde o surpriză, o rață ciudată are probleme cu ouatul, un măgar docil suferă de o copită dureroasă, iar o capră își rupe piciorul. Între timp, dr. Pol își începe ziua examinând 26 de cățeluși, dr. Lisa rezolvă cazul dispariției unei cozi, iar Dr. Nicole pleacă la vânătoare.
programmes.subtitle: Cățeluși la control
programmes.title: Doctor Pol

programmes.description: Sălbăticia din China, prin junglele sale, pădurile de bambus sau sus în munți, ascunde minuni despre care majoritatea dintre noi nici măcar nu știam că există. Această splendidă serie documentară vă poartă prin această lume de basm.
programmes.subtitle: Născut în sălbăticie
programmes.title: Împărățiile ascunse ale Chinei

programmes.description: Elefanții din China joacă un rol crucial în sănătatea și diversitatea pădurilor tropicale din Yunnan. Dar, odată cu creșterea populației umane, viața devine tot mai dificilă pentru aceste creaturi mărețe. Pe parcursul unui an, urmărim o mamă-elefant în timp ce își învață puiul cum să supraviețuiască în habitatul lor natural, în timp ce o altă turmă întreprinde o călătorie maraton.
programmes.subtitle: Elefanții din Yunnan
programmes.title: Imperiul sălbatic al Chinei

programmes.description: După ce fată o iapă, dr. Schroeder examinează puiul. Doctorii administrează o transfuzie de plasmă ca să crească șansele de supraviețuire ale mânzului. Înapoi la clinică, medicii examinează un stol de pui care manifestă o boală misterioasă, efectuează o operație oculară la o pisică și găsesc o nouă casă pentru trei cobai adorabili.

programmes.title: Familia de veterinari

programmes.description: Veterinarii Schroeder se grăbesc să diagnosticheze și să trateze un câine care se află în stare critică, după ce a fost lovit de o mașină. programmes.description: Recifurile de corali tropicali sunt un adevărat paradis colorat pentru scafandri, dar pentru locuitorii marini este o lume dură, în care vânătoarea este constantă. Delfinii vânează în grupuri, peștii-leu injectează venin, crevetele- călugăr are cea mai rapidă lovitură, iar sepiile se camuflează perfect înainte de a ataca. În apele înșelătoare, fiecare zi este o adevărată luptă pentru supraviețuire.

programmes.title: Prădătorii recifului

programmes.description: O echipă de oameni de știință călătorește în Noua Zeelandă pentru a studia rechinii mako din apele din jur. Un pescar local, care și-a petrecut jumătate din viață acolo, le dă sfaturi, iar succesul nu este departe: membrii expediției dau peste exemplare atât de mari încât nu-și pot crede ochilor.
